heuristics.title: The Master Cocci Rule
heuristics.rule: All medically significant spherical bacteria (cocci) are Gram-positive (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus), EXCEPT the Neisseria genus (N. meningitidis, N. gonorrhoeae), which are Gram-negative diplococci.
heuristics.explanation: Spherical bacteria in medical microbiology are predominantly Gram-positive cocci. When encountering Gram-negative diplococci, the primary clinical genus is Neisseria.

heuristics.title: The Master Bacilli Rule
heuristics.rule: Most medically significant bacilli (rods) are Gram-negative (enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic rods), EXCEPT five major Gram-positive rod groups: Bacillus, Clostridium, Corynebacterium, Listeria, and Mycobacterium.
heuristics.explanation: Gram-negative rods form the vast majority of enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic pathogens. Gram-positive bacilli are restricted to spore-formers (Bacillus, Clostridium), non-spore-formers (Corynebacterium, Listeria), and acid-fast Mycobacterium.

heuristics.title: The Endospore Genera Rule
heuristics.rule: Bacterial endospores are produced exclusively by two Gram-positive rod genera: Bacillus (aerobic spore-former) and Clostridium (obligate anaerobic spore-former).
heuristics.explanation: No Gram-negative bacteria and no Gram-positive cocci produce endospores. Sporulation is restricted to the aerobic genus Bacillus and the anaerobic genus Clostridium.

heuristics.title: The Anthrax Polypeptide Capsule Exception
heuristics.rule: Virtually all bacterial capsules are composed of polysaccharides (e.g. S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae, Klebsiella), EXCEPT Bacillus anthracis, whose capsule is uniquely composed of poly-D-glutamic acid (a polypeptide).
heuristics.explanation: The B. anthracis capsule is encoded by plasmid pXO2 and consists of D-glutamic acid polymer rather than carbohydrate, making it a critical diagnostic and biochemical exception.

heuristics.title: Bacteria Not Visualized by Standard Gram Stain
heuristics.rule: Certain medically important bacteria cannot be seen on standard light microscopy Gram stain: Treponema (too thin; requires darkfield/fluorescence), Mycobacterium (high mycolic acid lipid wall; requires acid-fast stain), and Mycoplasma (lacks peptidoglycan entirely).
heuristics.explanation: Lecture 1 Slide 32 identifies bacteria not visualized by Gram stain: spirochetes (Treponema) are too narrow for standard light microscopy; Mycobacteria resist water-soluble dyes due to lipid-rich walls; Mycoplasma completely lacks a peptidoglycan cell wall.

heuristics.title: Triple Sugar Iron (TSI) Diagnostic Principles
heuristics.rule: TSI agar contains 0.1% glucose, 1.0% lactose, and 1.0% sucrose with phenol red indicator: fermentation of glucose alone yields alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A); fermentation of lactose/sucrose yields acid slant / acid butt (A/A); non-fermenters yield alkaline slant / alkaline butt (K/K).
heuristics.explanation: Because glucose is present in one-tenth the concentration of lactose/sucrose, bacteria that ferment glucose alone exhaust it on the aerobic slant, which reverts to red (alkaline), while the anaerobic butt remains yellow (acid) [L3 p27, 29].
